and it corrects the family tree in 6 places. the finding four plots in a row michael rocco mazza's four grandparents were born in three towns - piedimonte etneo on etna, briatico on the tyrrhenian coast, and scilla on the strait - about six hundred kilometres apart, in families that had never met. they arrived in australia between 1949 and 1953 on four different sailings. they are buried in four consecutive plots . v-1026 sebastiano mazza 22 october 1920 - and, of the four quarters, the one the archive knows least about. 40 people placed at piedimonte etneo 1879 the earliest mazza birth with a date 7 mazza here who are joined to nothing the town piedimonte etneo means the foot of the mountain, and it is exactly that: a comune of the province of catania standing on the north-eastern slope of etna , above fiumefreddo and the alcantara valley, looking out at the ionian sea. the neighbouring towns in this archive - mascali , giarre , linguaglossa 's side of the mountain - are all within a few kilometres. living on etna is a recurring administrative fact, not a metaphor. in 1928 the eruption that destroyed the town of mascali - the only town etna has swallowed whole in modern times - happened eight years after sebastiano mazza was born here, and the archive records mascali as a birthplace for people in this family. the line that carries the name, and stops three men, and then nothing. generation 3 rosario mazza - born here, arrived fremantle 4 october 1949, died at brisbane and buried at nudgee . 1920-2002 four generations. it is the shortest of the four quarters by five generations, and the surname the whole archive is named after runs out at a man about whom precisely one fact is known: that he was salvatore's father. the hundred and eleven the family tree also contains 7 mazza of piedimonte etneo - mariano, leonardo, orazio, umberto, giuseppa, serena, graziella and the rest - who form a complete little world of their own: parents, children, marriages, cousins. not one record joins them to sebastiano's line. they are almost certainly the same family. a town of a few thousand people does not produce two unrelated mazza kindreds. but "almost certainly" is not a document, and the join has to be made by a record rather than by an assumption - rocco pizzarello, 32, fabbro - the ages check exactly at both ends. born 3 october 1855, he is thirty-six in july 1892 - which is what act 162 of that year says - and fifty-two in march 1908 , which is what the manifest says. his mother was a sofi, and so was his wife michele donato married maria sofi . his mother was nunziata sofi . the two families were tied twice over - and he named his daughter nunziata , for his own mother, exactly as calabrian custom predicts for a first daughter. nunziata donato carries her grandmother's name. and the next door, already open the act names candeloro donato but not his wife, and nunziata sofi but not her parents. both are in one document: domenico donato and nunziata sofi's own marriage . he was thirty-eight and she thirty-seven in october 1855, so they were born about 1817-18 and married most likely between 1838 and 1848. the tavole of the scilla marriages have now been read complete

a family assembled from three corners of the italian south, and the ships that carried it. this is an archive of the mazza of brisbane - and of the three southern italian towns they came out of, none of which had heard of the other two. it is not a pedigree: of the 592 people recorded here, all but a handful never continued the line. only 68 of them have a death recorded anywhere - which is a measure of how much of this tree is still undated rather than of who is still alive. this archive opened with the mazza name reaching back four generations and stopping at a man with no dates at all. one day in the sicilian registers took it to seven generations and mariano mazza and maria catalano , and joined a hundred and ten cousins to the line - every step a document. the same day cost the archive its other headline. the calabrian prostamo were said to run nine generations to 1697 . audited, they are documented to a sailor dead before 1886 , and asserted for four generations above him . it is a public archive with one rule: a living person is named and nothing more - q: the name what the surnames in this archive mean, roughly how common they are, and - the useful part - how much that tells you abo the name - the mazza archive skip to the content mazza, and the nine names around it the name what the surnames in this archive mean, roughly how common they are, and - the useful part - how much that tells you about whether two people who share one are related. mazza mazza is the italian for a club, a mace or a mallet, from the latin mattea . as a surname it was coined in all the usual ways at once: as a nickname for a strong or a violent man, as a trade name for someone who worked with a mallet or a maul, and - most often - from the medieval personal name mazzo , itself a short form of names like giacomazzo and tommazzo. it is one of the most widespread surnames in italy, found from lombardy to sicily, and it was coined independently many times over . there is no founding mazza family. two mazza households in the same sicilian town are much more likely to be related than two mazza in different provinces - but "much more likely" is a probability, and this archive does not publish probabilities as descents. that is precisely the situation at piedimonte etneo , where 118 mazza sit in two groups that no record joins. the others name here where it belongs what it is prostamo 82 briatico, vibo valentia rare, and concentrated. almost the whole italian distribution sits in a few calabrian comuni around vibo valentia. a rare surname in one small place is the best gift a genealogist gets: two prostamo of briatico almost certainly are related. polistena 44 scilla, reggio calabria a toponymic - from the town of polistena in the province of reggio calabria. it marks a family that moved from there, and was named for having done so. arena 39 scilla, reggio calabria very common across calabria and sicily; the registry's index answers it: michali mazza · death registration 14 november 1926 · 1926/c/3983 · father salvatori mazza · mother maria lecota . lecota is the index's rendering of nicotra - and the same search returns rosario mazza, born 1899 , whose parents are given in full as salvatore mazza and maria concetta nicotra . the same couple, spelled properly. so michele mazza was a son of salvatore mazza and maria nicotra , and therefore sebastiano mazza 's elder brother . he came out first, alone, at sixteen. he was dead within nineteen months. twenty-four years later his family followed him to the port he had landed at. the archive should say what it still cannot: whether anyone was waiting for sebastiano in 1949, and whether the family knew where the boy was buried. the index gives a date and a registration number, not a grave. c in the registration means a country event - he did not die in brisbane. four deaths, and what each one proves date name registration father mother 14 november 1926 michali mazza 1926/c/3983 salvatori mazza maria lecota 19 march 1986 rosario mazza (b. 1899) 1986/2455 salvatore mazza maria concetta nicotra 24 september 1963 maria nicotra mazza 1963/b/61348 john nicotra venera cassaneti 3 august 1968 mary rosa mazza 1968/b/936 sebastiano mazza domenica postamo 24 june 1928 helen mazza 1928/b/4850 john fimister jane stewart 8 june 1986 mario mazza 1986/4396 rosario mazz

and in looking for him the archive found rosario, and a generation above him nobody knew was there. the family tree says salvatore mazza was born at piedimonte etneo in 1879 , son of a rosario mazza about whom exactly one thing was known: that he existed. finding salvatore's act of birth was supposed to name rosario and settle everything. salvatore is not in the register - not in 1875, 1876, 1877, 1878, 1879, 1880, 1881 or 1882 at piedimonte etneo, nor at mascali or giarre in 1879. but the five mazza births that are there, and two marriage acts , have between them built three documented households , proved two of the men brothers , and reached a generation the family tree does not contain at all . the finding innocenzio mazza and domenica cavallaro a birth act names a father. a marriage act names both fathers and both mothers - which is why two marriages were worth more than five births. two of them, two years apart, name the same couple: 1874, atto 26 antonino mazza , di anni trentuno , bracciante, qui nato, figlio d'innocenzio , bracciante, e di domenica cavallaro , industriosa - marries concetta sciacca , 19, daughter of the late antonino sciacca and rosaria greco. 16 january 1876 salvatore and antonino are brothers - born about 1841 and 1843, both braccianti of piedimonte etneo, both sons of domenica cavallaro . two independent acts, two years apart, naming the same mother. innocenzio mazza and domenica cavallaro are the earliest mazza this archive can name from a document -
